 Order

Appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 being aggrieved by award dated 24/8/2004 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident claims Tribunal, Shivpuri in Claim Case No.77/2003; whereby, the Claims Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs. 12,31,960/- alongwith interest at the rate of 5% per annum to the claimants/respondents No. 1 to 5.

entities.text: Second Additional Motor Accident claims Tribunal, Shivpuri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The liability for payment of compensation amount was fixed on appellant/Insurance Company and respondents No. 7 and 8 jointly and severally.

2. Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 17/1/2003 when deceased Rakesh was waiting for bus to go his village at Guna Chungi Naka, it is alleged that due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No. 6, offending truck bearing registration No. MP08D9986 dashed Rakesh due to which he died on spot.
Therefore, wife and children of deceased moved a claim petition which has been partly allowed by the impugned award and they have been awarded a compensation as mentioned hereinabove.

Therefore, Insurance Company is before this Court, assailing the liability part of the impugned award.
3 . It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company that impugned award is contrary to the law and also contrary to the facts and material available on record as the oral and documentary evidence has not been appreciated in true perspective.
Insured vehicle was a goods carrying vehicle and was insured for carrying goods only.

According to FIR deceased Rakesh Balmiki alongwith Halke Ram, Radhe Shyam and one another was sitting in the offending vehicle at the time of accident and same is also proved by Insurance Company by evidence of Investigating Officer as a witness DW/3/1.
When deceased and others were sitting in the dumper, the Insurance Company was not liable to be fastened with the liability as the vehicle was being run against the terms and condition of the policy.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
6.
Appeal is filed by the Insurance Company on the ground of non- liability.

7. It is not in dispute that the respondent No. 6 has caused the accident by driving the vehicle dumper bearing registration No. MP08D9986 negligently and in this accident, death of Rakesh Balmiki was caused.
it is also an admitted facts that at the time of accident, the above vehicle was insured with the appellant/Insurance Company.
The dumper is a goods carrying vehicle and is insured as such.
Hence, carrying of passengers by this vehicle is not allowed.
The risk of passenger be it fare paying or gratuitous is not covered under the Insurance Policy.
8. It is contended by the claimants that at the time of accident, the deceased Rakesh Balmiki was standing on roadside and as the dumper turned turtle, it fell on him and he came under it.

In this regard two witnesses Halkeram and Radheshyam, who were sitting in the vehicle in question have The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt.Kiran And Ors. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122674935/
2 been examined.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt.Kiran And Ors. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But their testimony does not inspire much confidence.
As per the police papers on which the claimants have themselves relied upon for proving the accident, the deceased was travelling alongwith other persons in the vehicle at the time of accident.
The statements given by the above witnesses in the Tribunal are contrary to their police statements.
There is no reason for the police to prepare false papers and change the nature of the accident.
No complaint of any sort has been made against the concerned police Officer by the claimants or by the witnesses.
9.Thus, the statements made by above two witnesses do not find support from their police statement.

On the contrary, witnesses Sitaram, who has lodged the FIR and was the Cleaner on the vehicle in question, has clearly stated about the travelling in the vehicle by the deceased alongwith other persons.
His testimony is without any infirmity and hence, reliable.
Further the way in which the accident is said to be happened is not clear and reliable.
10. The first version mentioned in the police papers regarding the accident is quite reliable.
In this regard, judicial pronouncement of Apex Court in the matter of Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Premlata Shukla and Ors.,2007ACJ1928(SC) is noteworthy.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Premlata Shukla and Ors.,2007ACJ1928(SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It has been held in said case that the statements recorded in the Tribunal should be given weightage over police papers and FIR is not a substantive piece of evidence and it can be used for corroboration and contradiction of its maker,
but, they should be without any infirmity but the veracity and the reliability of such statements can be checked in the context of their previous statements.
11.

In the instant case, it is clear from police papers itself that their version remained the same from beginning to end and there are major contradictions in the statement of witnesses tried to be projected as eye witnesses.

12. As such, Insurance Company cannot be held liable for payment of compensation amount and further since deceased was not a third party, in such matter doctrine of pay and recover cannot be applied and owner of the vehicle alone is liable to pay damages to the claimants, as accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle.
If any amount is paid by the insurance company to the claimants, the insurance company is entitled to get back the same.

13. In the result, appeal is allowed to the extent indicated hereinabove and Insurance Company is exonerated from its liability and respondents No. 6 and 7 are fastened with the liability for making payment of the compensation amount.
Accordingly, the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated hereinabove.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
